summary:
H.R. 7266, the “Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act,” amends section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, codified at 42 U.S.C. § 18723, by striking and restating that section to reauthorize and revise the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program.

Restated section 40124(a) defines key terms, including “advanced cybersecurity technology” as technology, operational capability, or service—including computer hardware, software, or related assets—that improves an electric utility’s ability to protect against, detect, respond to, or recover from a cybersecurity threat. It incorporates by reference the definitions of “bulk-power system” in Federal Power Act § 215(a), “cybersecurity threat” in Homeland Security Act of 2002 § 2200, and “defense critical electric infrastructure” in Federal Power Act § 215A(a). “Eligible entity” includes rural electric cooperatives; electric utilities owned by political subdivisions of a State, including municipally owned utilities; electric utilities owned by agencies, authorities, corporations, or instrumentalities of one or more political subdivisions; not-for-profit entities partnered with at least six such entities; and investor-owned electric utilities selling less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year.

Restated section 40124(b) directs the Secretary to maintain the Program to provide technical assistance and award funding, including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes, to eligible entities for protection against, detection of, response to, and recovery from cybersecurity threats. Subsection (c) establishes program objectives: deployment of advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems and increased participation by eligible entities in cybersecurity threat information-sharing programs.

Under subsection (d), the Secretary must, subject to the availability of appropriations, provide technical assistance and award funding on a competitive or noncompetitive basis; develop award and assistance criteria; may enter into agreements with eligible entities to facilitate program objectives; and must establish a process to inform eligible entities of opportunities, to the extent practicable. The Secretary must prioritize eligible entities that the Secretary determines have limited cybersecurity resources, own assets critical to bulk-power system reliability, or own or operate defense critical electric infrastructure.

Subsection (e) deems information shared by or with Federal, State, Tribal, or local governments under the Program to be voluntarily shared information and exempts it from disclosure under 5 U.S.C. § 552 and analogous State, Tribal, or local open records, open meetings, sunshine, or similar laws. Subsection (f) authorizes, but does not appropriate, $250,000,000 for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to carry out the section.
